# Introduction

The distribution properties of coefficients of modular forms modulo primes have been a subject of considerable interest in analytic and algebraic number theory, particularly in connection with congruences, partition functions, and traces of singular moduli. A foundational contribution to this area was made by Bruinier and Ono, who provided a complete classification of half-integral weight cusp forms with integer Fourier coefficients whose coefficients fail to be equidistributed modulo odd primes $\ell$ according to the Katz-Sarnak-type prediction that governs generic behavior. More precisely, they identified precisely those forms for which the coefficients of the cusp form, when reduced modulo $\ell$, do not become equidistributed among the nonzero residue classes in the expected manner. Their classification rests on the theory of Galois representations attached to half-integral weight forms, exploiting the fact that non-generic behavior modulo a prime is intimately tied to the existence of a companion form with a very restrictive structure—typically forced to lie in a finite-dimensional space of forms of a specified type. This result has since served as a key tool in establishing distribution results for arithmetic functions of interest, most notably for the partition function and for traces of singular moduli.

The present paper extends the Bruinier-Ono classification theorem to a substantially more general setting. Specifically, we consider a broader class of half-integral weight modular forms with integer coefficients, and for all primes $p \geq 5$ we classify those forms for which the mod $p$ distribution property fails to hold. The central technical tool that allows this generalization is the Rankin-Cohen bracket construction, which permits us to systematically build new half-integral weight forms from pairs of modular forms while controlling the resulting Fourier coefficients and their reductions modulo $p$. By carefully analyzing how the Rankin-Cohen bracket interacts with the mod $p$ reduction map, we are able to lift the original Bruinier-Ono framework beyond cusp forms in the strictest sense, thereby obtaining a classification theorem that applies uniformly for every prime $p \geq 5$, subject to conditions in the same spirit as those imposed in the original work, but now formulated for a wider family of forms.

Having established this extended classification theorem as the main structural result of the paper, we turn to several applications that illustrate its scope and utility.

The first application concerns traces of singular moduli. These traces, defined as sums of values of the classical modular $j$-function (or related modular functions) evaluated at CM points associated with discriminants of imaginary quadratic orders, are known to satisfy striking congruences and distributional properties, many of which were first uncovered through their generating functions being half-integral weight modular forms. By applying our extended classification theorem to the relevant generating functions, we derive new distribution results for traces of singular moduli modulo every prime $p \geq 5$. These results identify precisely when and how the traces fail to equidistribute modulo $p$, thereby generalizing prior results that were often restricted to specific families of primes or discriminants.

The second application addresses the Hurwitz class number $H(n)$, a classical arithmetic function that counts equivalence classes of positive definite binary quadratic forms of discriminant $-n$, weighted appropriately. The generating function of the Hurwitz class numbers is a well-known example of a mock modular form of weight $3/2$, and its completion transforms as a suitable non-holomorphic half-integral weight form. Using our main theorem, we establish new distribution properties for $H(n)$ modulo every prime $p \geq 5$, extending and complementing existing results in the literature on congruences for the Hurwitz class number.

Finally, the paper investigates an analogue of Newman's conjecture in the setting of overpartitions. Newman's conjecture, originally formulated for the ordinary partition function $p(n)$, asserts that for every prime $\ell$ and every residue class $r$ modulo $\ell$, there are infinitely many $n$ for which $p(n) \equiv r \pmod{\ell}$. While significant progress has been made toward this conjecture for the classical partition function, comparatively less is known in the setting of overpartitions, whose generating function is likewise connected to half-integral weight modular forms. We formulate a natural analogue of Newman's conjecture for the overpartition function $\overline{p}(n)$ and, using the machinery developed in this paper, obtain partial results toward its resolution, providing further evidence for the expected mod $p$ distributional behavior of overpartitions for primes $p \geq 5$.

Taken together, these results demonstrate that the Rankin-Cohen bracket construction provides a powerful and flexible tool for extending classification-type theorems for half-integral weight modular forms beyond their originally intended scope, with consequences reaching across several distinct areas of number theory, from CM theory and class numbers to the combinatorics of partitions.

# On the Distribution of Coefficients of Half-Integral Weight Modular Forms Modulo Primes p ≥ 5

## 1. Introduction

The arithmetic of modular forms of half-integral weight has long been a rich source of congruences and distribution results for classically defined arithmetic functions. A particularly influential line of investigation began with the work of Bruinier and Ono, who studied the failure of a certain equidistribution property for the Fourier coefficients of half-integral weight cusp forms modulo odd primes. Their results, building on the theory of modular forms modulo primes developed by Serre, Swinnerton-Dyer, and later refined by Ono, Ahlgren, and others, gave a precise classification of those cusp forms of half-integral weight whose coefficients fail to be equidistributed among the residue classes modulo an odd prime $\ell$. This classification had striking consequences: it explained, in a conceptual way, congruences for the partition function, for traces of singular moduli, and for other coefficients of interest arising from the theory of harmonic Maass forms and mock modular forms.

The Bruinier–Ono theorem, however, was formulated specifically for cusp forms; the general theory of modular forms of half-integral weight (including forms with poles at the cusps, and more generally weakly holomorphic modular forms) was not directly addressed by their methods, which relied crucially on properties special to cusp forms, such as the Deligne bound and the structure of newforms under the Shimura correspondence. The purpose of the present paper is to extend the Bruinier–Ono classification to the setting of general half-integral weight modular forms — not necessarily cuspidal, and in particular allowing weakly holomorphic and mock modular forms — for all primes $p \geq 5$.

Our approach departs from the original Bruinier–Ono method in an essential way. Rather than working directly with the half-integral weight form in question, we exploit the **Rankin–Cohen bracket** construction to manufacture a new cusp form of half-integral weight to which the classical theory can be applied. Recall that for modular forms $f$ of weight $k$ and $g$ of weight $\ell$, the $n$-th Rankin–Cohen bracket $[f,g]_n$ is again a modular form, of weight $k + \ell + 2n$, and is a cusp form whenever either $f$ or $g$ is a cusp form (for $n \geq 1$). By choosing an auxiliary cusp form $g$ of appropriate integral weight and level, and forming the bracket $[f, g]_n$ with our given half-integral weight form $f$, we obtain a genuine cusp form of half-integral weight whose coefficients encode, in a controlled way, the coefficients of $f$ twisted by those of $g$. Applying the Bruinier–Ono classification (in its extended form, valid for all $p \geq 5$) to this new cusp form, and then unwinding the Rankin–Cohen bracket construction via an explicit combinatorial formula relating the coefficients of $[f,g]_n$ to those of $f$ and $g$, allows us to transfer distributional information back to the original form $f$.

This method has two significant advantages over a direct approach. First, it circumvents the need for $f$ itself to satisfy strong analytic properties (holomorphy at all cusps, boundedness of coefficients, etc.), since these properties are instead demanded of the auxiliary form $g$, which can be chosen freely from the rich supply of classical cusp forms of integral weight. Second, it produces uniform results for all primes $p \geq 5$, improving on the odd-prime restriction of the original theorem and, more importantly, providing an explicit and constructive route to new congruences.

### 1.1 Main results

Let $f(z) = \sum_{n} a(n) q^n$ (with $q = e^{2\pi i z}$) be a modular form of half-integral weight $\lambda + 1/2$ on $\Gamma_0(4N)$ (possibly with poles at cusps, i.e. weakly holomorphic), and fix a prime $p \geq 5$. Following the classical framework, we say that the coefficients $a(n)$ satisfy an **equidistribution property modulo $p$** if, for every residue class $r \pmod p$, the density of integers $n$ (in the support of $f$, subject to the usual congruence conditions coming from the theta-multiplier) for which $a(n) \equiv r \pmod p$ is $1/p$. The failure of this property is governed, as in the integral weight case, by the vanishing (or near-vanishing) of $f$ modulo $p$ upon application of Hecke operators $T_{p^2}$, together with the theory of the Shimura lift and half-integral weight newforms.

Our main theorem may be stated as follows.

**Theorem A.** *Let $p \geq 5$ be prime, and let $f$ be a modular form of half-integral weight on $\Gamma_0(4N)$ with algebraic (in fact rational) Fourier coefficients $a(n)$. Suppose that the coefficients of $f$ fail to be equidistributed modulo $p$ in the sense above. Then there is an explicit finite set of cusp forms $g_1, \dots, g_r$ of integral weight, and an explicit index $n_0$, such that the Rankin–Cohen bracket $[f, g_i]_{n_0}$, reduced modulo $p$, lies in the space spanned by forms associated to a single Galois orbit of eigenforms with complex multiplication, or is itself congruent to zero modulo $p$. Conversely, every such configuration gives rise to a form $f$ whose coefficients fail to be equidistributed modulo $p$.*

The precise formulation of Theorem A requires care in specifying the level, the choice of auxiliary form $g$, and the notion of "explicit" bounds on $n_0$ in terms of the weight and level of $f$; these details occupy the technical heart of the paper (Sections 3–5).

### 1.2 Applications

The utility of Theorem A is best illustrated through its applications, which form the second half of the paper.

**Traces of singular moduli.** Let $j(z)$ denote the classical modular function, and for a negative discriminant $-d$, let $\mathrm{Tr}(d)$ denote the trace of singular moduli, i.e., the sum of $j(z) - 744$ over $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$-equivalence classes of CM points of discriminant $-d$, suitably weighted. Zagier showed that the generating function of these traces is (up to normalization) a weakly holomorphic modular form of weight $3/2$. Using Theorem A, we determine precisely the primes $p \geq 5$ (and residue classes) for which the traces $\mathrm{Tr}(d)$ fail to equidistribute modulo $p$, extending known results (previously available only for a sporadic list of small primes, or under the odd-prime restriction of Bruinier–Ono) to a complete classification for all $p \geq 5$. We further give explicit examples exhibiting new congruences of the form
$$
\mathrm{Tr}(pn) \equiv 0 \pmod{p}
$$
for certain small primes $p$ not previously known to satisfy such congruences.

**Hurwitz class numbers.** Since the Hurwitz class number generating function $\mathcal{H}(z) = \sum_{n \geq 0} H(n) q^n$ is itself a mock modular form of weight $3/2$ (with shadow related to a unary theta function), our methods — after passing to a suitable completion and cusp form via the Rankin–Cohen bracket construction — yield new distribution results for $H(n)$ modulo all primes $p \geq 5$. In particular we exhibit, for several small primes $p$, explicit arithmetic progressions on which $H(n)$ is forced (mod $p$) into a proper subset of residues, a phenomenon not detectable by the classical Bruinier–Ono theorem due to its restriction to cusp forms.

**An analogue of Newman's conjecture for overpartitions.** Newman's conjecture, still open in general, asserts that the ordinary partition function $p(n)$ takes every residue class modulo every prime $m$ infinitely often, for every non-negative residue and every prime $m \geq 5$ (with an appropriate modification at small primes). The overpartition function $\overline{p}(n)$, whose generating function
$$
\sum_{n \geq 0} \overline{p}(n) q^n = \prod_{n \geq 1} \frac{(1+q^n)}{(1-q^n)} = \frac{\eta(2z)^{?}}{\eta(z)^{2}}
$$
is (up to a simple twist) essentially a modular form of weight $1/2$ on a suitable congruence subgroup, is a natural test case for an analogous conjecture. As a corollary of Theorem A, and using the explicit classification it provides, we prove:

**Theorem B.** *For every prime $p \geq 5$ and every residue class $r \pmod p$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that*
$$
\overline{p}(n) \equiv r \pmod p.
$$

This resolves, for all primes $p \geq 5$, the natural analogue of Newman's conjecture for the overpartition function, complementing earlier partial results (which were confined to small primes or to specific residues) and demonstrating the strength of the Rankin–Cohen bracket technique introduced here.

### 1.3 Organization of the paper

In Section 2 we recall the necessary background on modular forms of half-integral weight, the Shimura correspondence, the theory of modular forms modulo primes, and the original Bruinier–Ono theorem. In Section 3 we develop the Rankin–Cohen bracket technique in the half-integral weight setting, establishing the key coefficient formula that allows us to relate the mod $p$ behavior of $f$ to that of $[f,g]_n$. Section 4 is devoted to the proof of Theorem A. Section 5 contains the applications to traces of singular moduli and Hurwitz class numbers, including explicit numerical examples. Section 6 proves Theorem B on overpartitions, and we conclude in Section 7 with some remarks on possible extensions of the method to primes $p = 2, 3$ and to forms of higher half-integral weight not treated here.

Recently, Bruinier and Ono obtained a remarkable finite algebraic formula for the partition function $p(n)$, resolving a longstanding problem in the theory of partitions. Prior to their work, the only known effective methods for computing $p(n)$ relied either on the Hardy–Ramanujan–Rademacher exact formula, which expresses $p(n)$ as an infinite (though rapidly converging) series involving Kloosterman sums and Bessel functions, or on generating function techniques that do not readily reveal arithmetic structure. Bruinier and Ono instead showed that $p(n)$ can be realized as a finite sum of algebraic numbers, arising as traces of singular moduli associated to a certain weak Maass form of weight $-1/2$.

Their approach builds on the theory of harmonic Maass forms and mock modular forms, which had been developed extensively by Zagier, Bruinier, Ono, and others in the years following Zwegers' thesis on Ramanujan's mock theta functions. The key object in their construction is a specific weak Maass form $Q(z)$ whose coefficients are governed by a generating function closely related to the partition generating function. By evaluating a certain modular function at Heegner points associated to imaginary quadratic discriminants $-24n+1$, Bruinier and Ono produced explicit algebraic numbers whose sum, after simplification, yields precisely $p(n)$. Remarkably, this construction places the partition function within the same conceptual framework used to study traces of singular moduli for the $j$-invariant, a subject with deep roots in the work of Zagier and Borcherds on Heegner points and Borcherds products.

Beyond providing a strikingly different way of computing partition numbers, the Bruinier–Ono formula illuminates connections between partitions, modular forms, and the theory of complex multiplication that were previously unsuspected. Their result has since inspired a number of generalizations, including analogous algebraic formulas for other combinatorial and number-theoretic functions expressible via mock modular forms, as well as further investigations into the arithmetic properties of harmonic Maass forms. The techniques introduced in their paper — particularly the use of regularized theta lifts and the interplay between weakly holomorphic modular forms and their shadows — have become standard tools in the modern study of mock modular forms and their applications to partitions, $L$-functions, and moonshine phenomena.

# Research Abstract

**On the Distribution of Half-Integral Weight Modular Forms Modulo Odd Primes and Applications to Overpartition Functions**

We establish an extension of a classical distribution theorem for half-integral weight modular forms modulo odd primes $\ell \geq 5$, generalizing prior results of Ono and collaborators that characterized the vanishing and non-vanishing of Fourier coefficients in arithmetic progressions. Building on the theory of Galois representations attached to half-integral weight cusp forms and the Shimura correspondence, we show that for a broad class of forms $f(z) = \sum_{n \geq 0} a(n) q^n \in M_{\lambda + 1/2}(\Gamma_0(N), \chi)$ satisfying suitable congruence conditions, the coefficients $a(n)$ are equidistributed modulo $\ell$ with respect to a natural filtration determined by the associated Hecke eigenform and its mod $\ell$ Galois representation. Our approach refines the nilpotency and density arguments of the Serre–Ono framework by incorporating twisted Shimura lifts and explicit computations of local representations at $\ell$, allowing us to remove certain restrictive hypotheses on the level and character present in earlier work.

As a primary application, we resolve new cases in the study of the divisibility properties of the overpartition function $\overline{p}(n)$, proving that for infinitely many primes $\ell$, the overpartition function satisfies
$$\overline{p}(An + B) \equiv 0 \pmod{\ell}$$
for explicitly determined arithmetic progressions $An+B$, extending known results for $\ell \in \{3,5,7\}$ to a wider family of primes and providing the first systematic density estimates for such congruences. In particular, we determine the proportion of integers $n$ for which $\overline{p}(n) \equiv 0 \pmod \ell$, showing this density is $100\%$ within any fixed arithmetic progression satisfying our hypotheses.

As a further application, we make progress toward Newman's conjecture on the equidistribution of the ordinary partition function $p(n)$ modulo every prime $\ell \geq 5$. Using the extended distribution theorem, we verify Newman's conjecture for several new primes and residue classes, and we prove a partial equidistribution result establishing that each nonzero residue class modulo $\ell$ is attained by $p(n)$ with positive density, conditional on standard conjectures concerning the non-vanishing of central $L$-values for twists of the relevant half-integral weight forms. These results strengthen the connection between the arithmetic of modular forms of half-integral weight and open conjectures in the theory of integer partitions, and suggest further avenues for attacking Newman's conjecture in full generality via refined multiplicity-one statements for mod $\ell$ Galois representations.

Using the theory of Rankin–Cohen brackets, we construct new families of modular forms whose coefficients encode combinatorial and arithmetic data, including generalized class numbers $H(N)$ and overpartition functions $\overline{p}(n)$. 

By analyzing the images of these forms under the $\xi$-operator and exploiting the interplay between holomorphic projection and the theory of Poincaré series, we obtain explicit formulas relating the coefficients of Rankin–Cohen brackets to twisted traces of singular moduli and to central values (and derivatives) of quadratic twists of $L$-functions. Finally, we discuss how the nonvanishing of these brackets modulo primes $\ell$ can be interpreted in terms of the non-triviality of certain classes in the Shimura correspondence, providing further evidence for conjectural relationships between periods of half-integral weight forms and $\ell$-adic Galois representations attached to modular forms of even weight.
